STAGE 1 - read the task and the three frozen bundles; goal: ground every dimension in an evidence id rather than in the proposal's own rhetoric.
READ: rubric-2026-10-v1 anchors; bundles 404ea254563870a6 (SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ), bc19762831440f87 (cocond-markov-poincare-ot), e9e97242e0e9ed08 (CURVCELL-SID). All three share the same OBSERVED block E4-E11, differing only in PROPOSED E1-E3 and E12-E13.
OBSERVED: E5 successor-entropy stratification (bin1 top1 mass .4375, H .931, 4895 items; bin5 top1 .0543, H 3.405, support 44.3); E6 beam survival (l1_br .04671, l1_br_euclid .06207, l1_only .06233, resample .06363, successor_entropy .05122, geodesic_coarse .05500, v2 .05463, tangent_successor_residual .05500; all below the 0.065 target, best .06363); E7 per-position NLL; E8 first-level capacity ceiling (K=16 .3106 vs negative .1352; K=256 .0822 vs .0129); E9 cohort profile (.9291 vs .8871, n=52855); E10 distinct_edges 115582, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526, items ~24556; E11 same_first_prefix_rate .0907 vs permuted null .067.
REASONING: two facts drive most of my scoring. (i) E10 gives the transition graph density, which lets me compute whether a 1024x1024 batch-restricted diffusion operator carries any mass at all. (ii) E8 says that at level 1, COARSE cells co-locate behavioural neighbours far more often in absolute terms than fine cells (0.3106 at K=16 vs 0.0822 at K=256), which cuts directly against the "hub prefixes need MORE resolution" premise of SUCCFAN.
OPEN: whether each candidate's off-switches are separable, and whether the curvature enters as anything other than a per-point/per-code scalar weight.

STAGE 2 - SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ scoring, checked by hand against the arithmetic of the conformal factor.
READ: bundle 404ea254563870a6 E1-E13; E12 gives lambda_p(x)=2/(1-c_p||x||^2), c_p in (0.1,10.0); E13 (where it acts) is EMPTY in the bundle, so the assignment-score form is only named ("conformal approximation"), never written.
OBSERVED / derived: (a) at c=0, lambda=2/(1-0)=2, NOT 1, so the declared geometry-off arm ("c->0 gives lambda==1, plain RQ sum") is arithmetically false; a global x2 residual multiplier is not the identity. (b) with c up to 10 and ||x||<=1, 1-c||x||^2 changes sign at ||x||=1/sqrt(c); e.g. c=10, ||x||=0.5 gives 1-2.5=-1.5 and lambda=-1.333, and lambda -> +-inf as c||x||^2 -> 1. (c) encode multiplies by lambda, decode divides by lambda, so the level-l error in original units is ||lambda r - c_k||/lambda: this is a per-node effective step size, i.e. a per-node Euclidean scalar, exactly reproducible by a matched Euclidean control.
REASONING: behaviour evidence 3 - E5 measures fanout heterogeneity with support, but the SID-side claim (hubs need finer residual) is not measured and E8 points the other way. geometry 2 - a scalar multiplier, no distance/exp/log; matched Euclidean per-node scale reproduces it. novelty 2 - per-branch/per-node curvature from branching is already in the ledger (cocond's own novelty paragraph names "per-branch curvature"). downstream 3 - scaling a residual moves the query radially; it does not place codes on successor groups. falsifiability 3 - the geometry-off control is mis-specified (lambda=2). implementability 2 - f_i -> c_p map absent, assignment score absent, E13 empty, singular range unguarded. exploration 2 - a granularity change of a measured family, and E8 predicts the wrong direction.
OPEN: nothing further without the real Stage-2 code; the arithmetic checks are decisive for the controls.

STAGE 3 - cocond-markov-poincare-ot scoring; checked the diffusion mass against the graph density and the Sinkhorn iterates against the argmax.
READ: bundle bc19762831440f87 E1-E13; spec steps (1)-(6); SAFEGUARDS referenced for alpha and q but not included; E10 mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526, distinct_edges 115582; batch B=1024, item count ~24556.
DERIVED (the decisive one): expected in-batch successors per row = 5.4526 * (1024/24556) = 0.227. So B_bt has ~0.23 nonzeros per row. Either it is unnormalised, in which case (1-alpha)P + alpha*B_bt P shrinks the row and the following row-normalisation gives back ~P (mixing weight ~alpha*0.23), or it is normalised on in-batch mass only, in which case the "Markov step" is estimated from fewer than one edge. Either way the behaviour switch is close to inert at the frozen batch size.
DERIVED (second): the last operation of each sweep, P <- P*(q/max(colsum(P),eps)), multiplies every entry of column j by one positive scalar, so the row argmax over j is unchanged by it; and P <- P/max(rowsum) is a uniform row scale, also argmax-invariant. Columns never mix under B_bt @ P. Hence the "entropic OT plan" argmax is a column-rescaled, column-independently smoothed cost, and the marginals never converge - the transport reading is cosmetic.
REASONING: behaviour 4 (E11 .0907 vs permuted null .067 plus E9/E10 shows the SID carries almost no successor structure, measured). geometry 2 (Poincare distance is cosh d = 1+2||p-c||^2/((1-||p||^2)(1-||c||^2)), a monotone function of a per-point/per-code weighted Euclidean distance; the Klein Einstein midpoint is a weighted Euclidean mean in Klein coordinates, i.e. a fixed reparametrisation), so a matched Euclidean weighted quantiser reproduces the ordering. novelty 3 (moving the assignment plan is a different operator from the ledger's losses/latents, but "per-branch curvature" is not traceably separated and no ids are cited). downstream 4 (diffusing cost across transition edges directly targets prefix sharing). falsifiability 4 (three switches, criterion, diagnostics, refutation cases). implementability 2 (alpha and q undefined - SAFEGUARDS absent; the batch-restricted operator needs a redesign to carry any mass). exploration 3.
OPEN: whether a full-graph or kNN-gathered diffusion (instead of B_bt) would restore the intended mechanism - that is the bounded check that would settle implementability.

STAGE 4 - CURVCELL-SID scoring; checked whether the two off-switches are separable and whether d_B/s is geometric.
READ: bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08 E1-E13; spec: s[l][k]=sqrt(kappa[l][k]), s_new=log(1+B)/((d-1)R), distance d_B(eps,c)/s, refresh at epochs 1,2,4,...,2048, beta inherited, clamp (bound unstated).
DERIVED: s IS sqrt(kappa), so "geometry-off keeps the behaviour weights but removes curvature" has no referent - keeping the weights keeps the curvature, dropping them sets s=1 which is exactly behaviour-off. The 2x2 switch design therefore collapses to one off-arm, so the behaviour and geometry factors cannot be attributed separately.
DERIVED: d_B(eps,c)/s_k with cosh d_B = 1+2||eps-c||^2/((1-||eps||^2)(1-||c||^2)) is a strictly increasing function of ||eps-c||^2 * a_eps * b_c, divided by the per-code constant s_k; so the argmin equals a per-code weighted Euclidean argmin with scale 1/s_k. A matched Euclidean per-code scale reproduces it exactly.
DERIVED (direction): s grows with log(1+B), so a high-branching code has a SMALLER scaled distance and claims MORE items. The predicted fall in H(next code | level-0 code) does not follow: giving a level-0 code more mass pushes more items into its subtree, which by itself raises the conditional entropy over the level-1 codes.
REASONING: behaviour 4 (E8 K=16 .3106 vs K=256 .0822 with the same fixed negatives, plus E5 branching bins, gives a measured first-level capacity ceiling; the coarse-is-better direction even supports CURVCELL's "size the cell by branching"). geometry 2. novelty 3 (the co-evolving fixed-point refresh is the only element not already in the per-branch-curvature ledger). downstream 3 (cell SIZE, not cell placement, is what the behaviour sets; the assignment change is real but the successor alignment step is missing). falsifiability 3 (off-switches coincide). implementability 4 (complete pseudocode, no gradient into s, eps guard, derived refresh schedule, 1-2 s per refresh, +2..4% step; the clamp bound is unstated). exploration 3.
OPEN: the clamp target for s and whether empty/non-convex cells actually occur are the two bounded checks I cannot run here.

STAGE 5 - final answer complete; three blocks, scores and verdicts.
SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ: be3 gn2 nov2 dm3 fal3 imp2 ex2, IN_SCOPE. lambda is a per-node scalar (decoded error ||lambda r - c||/lambda); lambda(c=0)=2 not 1 so the geometry-off control is broken; lambda=-1.333 at c=10,||x||=0.5; E8 points the opposite way to "finer for hubs".
cocond-markov-poincare-ot: be4 gn2 nov3 dm4 fal4 imp2 ex3, IN_SCOPE. Batch-restricted diffusion carries 5.4526*1024/24556=0.227 in-batch successors per row => behaviour switch near inert; column scaling in the Sinkhorn leaves the row argmax invariant, so the plan is not a transport plan; Poincare distance reduces to a per-point weighted Euclidean ordering.
CURVCELL-SID: be4 gn2 nov3 dm3 fal3 imp4 ex3, IN_SCOPE. s=sqrt(kappa) is the curvature, so geometry-off and behaviour-off coincide; d_B/s reduces to a per-code scaled Euclidean argmin; larger s for high-branching codes claims more mass and raises, not lowers, H(next code|level-0 code).
Uncertainty carried: the 0.227 figure depends on N=24556 and B=1024; clamp bound and empty-cell rate unmeasured.

STAGE: score cocond-markov-poincare-ot (proposal 2 of 3)
GOAL: decide scope, score the seven dimensions, and record the strongest objection and a minimal counterexample for the successor-diffused Sinkhorn/OT proposal.
READ: frozen bundle bc19762831440f87 (E1-E13) and the proposal text.
OBSERVED: behaviour is a popularity-adjusted directed transition matrix from the Stage-2 split, used as the Markov diffusion operator inside the entropic-OT assignment plan, E1-E3; curvature enters the Sinkhorn ground cost (Poincare distance) and the codebook step (Klein/Einstein weighted barycenter), E12-E13. Direct support that prefixes carry almost no successor structure: same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067, E11; transition edges 118315 over 115582 distinct pairs with mean out-degree 5.45 and density 5.33 over sampled users, E10; beam containment for the Euclidean control is only 0.0847 with depth-3/4 survival 0.161/0.085, E6.
REASONING: behaviour_evidence=4 (E11 measures the SID-side claim directly, E10 covers the graph, but coverage is sampled-user-only so 5 is not reachable). geometry_necessity=3: the Poincare cost and the Klein closed-form barycenter are genuinely non-Euclidean operators, but no matched Euclidean control (same Sinkhorn+diffusion with squared Euclidean cost and weighted Euclidean mean) is specified or ruled out. novelty=4: it enumerates the ledger families and the difference is computational (it moves the assignment plan, not the latent or a loss), though no external OT/hyperbolic-clustering prior art is cited. downstream=4: the assignment change, the expected direction (prefix hit rate up, conditional code entropy down, recall up) and the diagnostics are named; the gap is that beam containment, not prefix co-location, may bind, E6/E7. falsifiability=4 (alpha=0 and kappa->0 removals plus the explicit decorative-structure criterion), implementability=3 (alpha and q are deferred to an unseen SAFEGUARDS section; B_bt zero-row convention unspecified; the cost line ignores the BxB@BxK MACs if the operator is dense), exploration=4.
KEY QUANTITATIVE OBJECTION: with B=1023 sampled from 24556 items and mean out-degree 5.45, about 80% of rows have no successor inside the mini-batch ((1-0.0417)^5.45 ~ 0.80); for those rows B_bt[i,:]=0, so P<-(1-alpha)P+alpha(B P) is a uniform row shrink followed by the column rescale q/colsum, and the transition signal collapses to the static usage prior. Minimal counterexample: row i with no in-batch successor and uniform q => argmax_j P_ij = argmax_j P^0_ij, i.e. the plain Poincare-cost argmax, identical under behaviour-on and behaviour-off.
SCOPE: IN_SCOPE. Missing only the explicit switch flags and a geometry-off arm that retains the diffusion; the HYPOTHESIS names the both-off Euclidean baseline rather than the geometry-off arm.
OPEN: the exact in-batch edge density under the frozen sampler is UNKNOWN; a one-batch count would resolve it.

STAGE: score CURVCELL-SID (proposal 3 of 3)
GOAL: decide scope, score the seven dimensions, and record the strongest objection and a minimal counterexample for the self-consistent per-code curvature field.
READ: frozen bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08 (E1-E13) and the proposal text.
OBSERVED: behaviour is the effective number of distinct successor code-groups B[l][k] per current cell, from training transitions only, E1-E3; curvature kappa[l][k]=(log(1+B)/((d-1)R))^2 enters the Poincare distance divided by s=sqrt(kappa), the commitment term and the Mobius residual, E12-E13; fanout heterogeneity is measured, E5, and transition coverage is E10; E8 measures that a coarser first level keeps behavioural neighbours together more often (K=16 share 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822); E6 gives depth 3/4 prefix survival 0.161/0.085.
REASONING: behaviour_evidence=4 (E5/E10 support the branching premise, but the cell-level B[l][k] distribution that the mechanism consumes is UNKNOWN; the bounded check is to compute B[l][k] on the baseline SIDs and report its spread). geometry_necessity=2: D=2*atanh(||(-eps)(+)c||)/s is a monotone Mobius distance divided by a per-code scalar, which a matched Euclidean ||eps-log_0(c)||/s reproduces up to the atanh distortion, and d/s is not even a metric. novelty=3 (the self-consistent fixed point is a real difference from a static per-branch curvature, but the family is in the ledger). downstream=3: the direction claim "H(next code | level-0 code) falls" is contradicted by the mechanism's own cell-size rule (larger s for high-B codes => larger cell => more mass on the highest-entropy cells). falsifiability=4 (three clean matched arms, explicit Spearman(|A_k|,B_k)~0 failure criterion, and what would refute). implementability=4 (complete equations, measured R, derived refresh schedule, negligible cost, clamps; missing the codebook update rule under a non-metric distance, the empty-cell q[m], and a derived clamp bound). exploration=3.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: a level-0 cell k containing only items with 8 successor code-groups gets B=8, hence the largest s_k=log9/((d-1)R), hence the smallest d/s_k and the largest claim on new items; its next-code distribution is spread over 8 groups by construction (H=log 8=2.08 nats, the maximum), and the aggregate H=sum_k w_k H_k rises in w_k, so H can increase while Spearman(|A_k|,B_k)>0 holds.
SCOPE: IN_SCOPE; nothing missing for the gate, but the geometry-off arm ("keeps behaviour weights, removes curvature") has to be implemented as a Euclidean distance scaled by the same s, which the text only describes.
OPEN: empty-cell handling and the clamp bound are not determined by the text.

STAGE: FINAL ANSWER (compressed to the 4000-char record limit; the full seven-line blocks are in the response).

SCOPE: SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ | IN_SCOPE | behaviour E1-E3, curved object E12-E13, one pathway; caveat: geometry-off c->0 also disables behaviour.

STAGE: scoring block 1 of 3 (reviewer scoring_2, rubric-2026-10-v1). GOAL: score SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ on seven dimensions, scope verdict, evidence, objection, counterexample.
READ: proposal text (fanout -> per-prefix c_p -> lambda_p=2/(1-c_p||x||^2) multiplying the level-l RQ residual at encode, dividing at decode) plus evidence bundle 404ea254563870a6: E5 (successor-entropy quintiles: top-1 mass 0.4375 -> 0.0543, Spearman -0.9733, per-bin item counts and support), E10 (edge counts, mean out-degree 5.4526, coverage note), E11 (same-first-prefix 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067), E6 (width-20 beam survival, euclid 0.06207, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500), E8 (K=256 -> 0.0822 pair share, K=16 -> 0.3106), E12/E13 (curved operation: conformal factor; bundle text itself truncated at "conformal approximatio...").
